findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple employees switch tasks between food prep and handling monetary transactions or touching their sides without hand washing. CORRECTED- inspector modeled and discussed appropriate times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC) and food handlers. A failure to wash hands before donning gloves allows contaminants on one’s bare hands to transfer to the food contact surfaces of the otherwise clean gloves. Ensure employees always wash hands before donning gloves and in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the front counter to have a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia (quat). CORRECTED- the PIC remade the sanitizer to a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary. Ensure sanitizing solutions are made at a frequency to hold the proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed strawberries and blueberries on the “toast line” to be out of temperature (strawberries probed at 61.8F and blueberries probed at 60F). PIC stated that both the strawberries and blueberries had been placed on the line around 8am (inspection began at 1pm- 5 hours past the items were taken from the cooler), and held on ice packs. CORRECTED- the blueberries and strawberries were voluntarily discarded by the operator. Inspector and PIC discussed using a different method for cold holding items on the toast line in the future- either ice, or implementing time as control (TAC). If TAC were implemented, items would be used or discarded every 4 hours. If using ice for cold holding, it is recommended that that be refreshed every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: The handles of multiple in-use scoops at the smoothie prep station were observed touching the food powder. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the handles above the surface with a clean, gloved hand, and reminded food handlers to keep the handles above the food. Ensure that food with handles are always stored with the food contact surfaces in the food, and the handles are stored above the food to avoid bare hand contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets on the double door cooler to be separating. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Replace or repair gaskets by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) Inspector observed food debris in the prep cooler as well as the standing freezer in the kitchen.
2) Inspector observed a significant accumulation of ice in the chest freezer. Routinely clean during defrost cycles.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
No CFM was present during this inspection. Multiple priority and priority foundation violations were observed during this inspection, including improper handwashing technique, improper use of handwashing sinks, and inadequate sanitizing procedures. Inspector will follow up to see that staff are educated on proper handwashing and sanitizing procedures.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There was no certified food protection manager present during this inspection. Ensure sufficient staff are certified food protection managers and are scheduled to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employees were observed to wash hands then turn the faucet off without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- Discussed proper handwashing procedure with employees present. Review handwashing procedure with all employees. Use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The back handwashing sink was observed being used to rinse strawberries, with a container of strawberries sitting in the sink basin. Handwashing sinks are to be used only for handwashing. Educate employees to use handwashing sinks only for their designated handwashing purpose.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Smoothie blender cups are rinsed with water after each use. When asked about sanitizing procedures, employees reported that they are sanitized nightly. In-use food contact surfaces (such as the blender cups) need to be cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours. There is a tracking chart posted on the drive-thru window side of the sprayer sink splash guard. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed with the employees present. Blender cups were removed to be washed, rinsed, sanitized, and allowed to air dry before returning to use.
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
The dipping well is not holding sufficient water to cover the scoops and wash away debris. Repair the dipping well so it holds enough water to submerge the scoops. In the meantime, ensure that in-use scoops are washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Food debris accumulation was observed in the chest freezer. Ensure freezer interiors are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.  [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler certificates were not available for two of the 3 employees present during this inspection. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire (and renew as needed). Keep certificates available on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]
